source: Temporal Durable Execution for AI Agents
summary: Journal-based replay and DB checkpointing pattern for fault-tolerant agentic pipelines; validated at scale by Temporal ($300M raise, 9.1T executions). LangGraph/Pydantic AI/OpenAI SDK all adopted this as first-class feature in 2025-2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses the AIBlocked dead-end with no auto-recovery; stage checkpointing maps cleanly onto the deterministic state machine

source: PROJECTMEM: A Local-First, Event-Sourced Memory and Judgment Layer for AI Coding Agents
summary: Append-only event log of typed coding events (issue, attempt, fix, decision) projected into compact AI-readable summaries + Memory-as-Governance pre-action gate that warns agents before repeating known failures. 5k-20k token savings per session; 207 events across 10 projects over 2 months.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses 'no agent memory across runs'; event types map to AgentForge stage transitions; pre-action gate fits policyEngine.ts

source: AgentFactory: A Self-Evolving Framework Through Executable Subagent Accumulation and Reuse
summary: Preserves successful task solutions as executable Python subagents; reuses and refines them on similar tasks, achieving 57% orchestration cost reduction on repeat task types. Presented at ACL 2026 Demo Track.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — plan library concept maps directly to AgentForge's artifact model; auto-promoting proven plans before the Planning stage reduces Claude tokens on repetitive tasks

source: PASTE: Act While Thinking — Pattern-Aware Speculative Tool Execution
summary: Mines recurring tool-call patterns from execution traces, speculatively pre-executes predicted tools while model is still thinking. 48.5% latency reduction, 48.6%/61.9% p95/p99 tail latency reduction. By SJTU + Microsoft Research, March 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — compelling latency gains but conflicts with AgentForge's strictly sequential single-agent-per-stage model; would require significant architecture change to ProcessRunner

source: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
summary: Coding agent that recursively self-improves via open-ended evolutionary code changes using foundation models to propose modifications, then evaluating on benchmarks. Experiments show improvement scales with compute.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — architecturally inspiring but too experimental and large in scope for 1-2 sprint implementation; requires external evaluation harness and significant infrastructure

source: Memanto: Typed Semantic Memory with Information-Theoretic Retrieval for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: 13-category typed semantic memory schema with no-indexing information-theoretic retrieval; achieves 89.8% on LongMemEval and 87.1% on LoCoMo, beating hybrid graph+vector systems. Sub-90ms retrieval latency. April 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — strong memory architecture but PROJECTMEM's coding-agent-specific event types and pre-action gate were more directly applicable; Memanto is better suited to dialogue agents

source: Cost-Aware Speculative Execution for LLM-Agent Workflows: An Integrated Five-Dimension Method
summary: Five-dimension framework (latency/cost tradeoff, per-token billing, Bayesian success estimation, failure-weighted cost term, admissibility precondition) for cost-aware speculative execution in LLM workflows. By AWS, June 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — excellent cost modeling but requires speculative execution infrastructure that AgentForge does not have; too many architectural prerequisites

source: B-PASTE: Beam-Aware Pattern-Guided Speculative Execution for Resource-Constrained LLM Agents
summary: Extension of PASTE that adds beam-search-style multi-branch speculation under resource constraints. Optimizes for cost as well as latency. April 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — builds on PASTE which itself was not selected; resource-constrained variant is even further from AgentForge's current sequential architecture

source: SPORK: Self-Speculative Forking to Accelerate Agentic LLM Inference
summary: Self-speculative forking that branches the agent's own inference at decision points, evaluating multiple continuations and merging the best. July 2026, very new.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — novel forking mechanism but extremely new (July 2026) and requires major inference-level changes; worth re-evaluating when it matures

source: Progressive Crystallization: Turning Agent Exploration into Deterministic, Lower-Cost Workflows in Production
summary: Methodology for crystallizing successful agent exploration traces into deterministic, cheaper production workflows. July 2026, very new.
relevanceToAgentForge: High potential — complements plan template library idea; watch for more details as this could inform how AgentForge promotes and solidifies reusable patterns

source: DemoEvolve: Overcoming Sparse Feedback in Agentic Harness Evolution with Demonstrations
summary: Uses demonstrations to bootstrap agent harness evolution when execution feedback is sparse; addresses the cold-start problem in self-evolving agent frameworks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — relevant to the plan template library when run history is thin; technique could improve cold-start quality of template retrieval

source: Sherlock: Reliable and Efficient Agentic Workflow Execution
summary: Reliability framework for agentic workflows with structured error handling and fallback strategies. November 2025 paper.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — general reliability patterns; superseded by more specific Temporal-pattern implementation chosen for HID-177
